Hero.description: PyAnimate blends a browser playground, visual execution, guided prompts, and level-based tracks so you can build Python intuition faster.

Outcomes.traceDesc: See variables, loops, and stack transitions instead of reading raw output alone.
Outcomes.practiceDesc: Move through clear tracks with pacing from first syntax to advanced algorithms.
Outcomes.experimentDesc: Edit live, replay execution, and understand mistakes before they harden into habits.

TrackGrid.heading: Progress from first print statement to expert-level reasoning.

LearningJourney.clickHint: Click any step to open the track

AlgorithmPipeline.heading: Every algorithm follows the same pipeline.

LessonSpotlight.heading: See algorithms run, not just read about them.
LessonSpotlight.description: Each lesson animates the execution path step by step, then gives you a challenge to modify and rerun.

Playground.headline: Learn, edit, replay, and understand each step before moving on.
Playground.subheadline: The playground auto-runs on load. Hit {runMyCode} to trace your own Python — every step animated live.
Playground.memoryMatrixHint: Run the timeline to visualize blocks mapping into memory space.

foundation.description: Start from zero. Learn how Python thinks about data, decisions, and flow — step by step, with every concept animated.

beginner.description: Build real programming habits. Master loops, functions, and lists by watching them execute one step at a time.

intermediate.description: Upgrade your toolkit. Explore dictionaries, stacks, queues, and your first search algorithms with visual state tracking.

advanced.description: Think algorithmically. See sorting and tree algorithms animate in real time, understand Big O through observation.

mastery.description: Push to the frontier. Graph search, dynamic programming, and interview-level algorithms — all visualized live.

algorithms.hello-world: Your first Python output. See how print() sends data to the console and why it's the foundation of all debugging.
algorithms.variables-types: Watch a variable come to life in memory. See int, float, str, and bool as living boxes that hold values.
algorithms.string-operations: Strings are sequences. See slicing, concatenation, and methods animate over character arrays.
algorithms.arithmetic: Numbers, operators, and integer division. See exactly how Python evaluates expressions step by step.
algorithms.if-else: Code that makes decisions. Watch execution jump between branches based on truthiness.
algorithms.while-loop: Repetition driven by a condition. See the loop guard check before every iteration and why infinite loops happen.
algorithms.for-loop: Iterate over sequences. See how Python's for loop is really an iterator under the hood.
algorithms.lists-basics: Python's most useful container. See append, pop, and index as operations on an animated memory block.
algorithms.functions-intro: Reusable blocks of logic. Watch a function call push a stack frame and return value flow back to the caller.
algorithms.input-output: Programs that talk to users. See how input() pauses execution and returns a string value.
algorithms.linear-search: Check every element until you find the target. O(n) — the simplest search algorithm there is.
algorithms.count-occurrences: Count how many times a value appears. See a hash map accumulate counts with each pass.
algorithms.find-min-max: Track the running minimum and maximum through a single pass. See why one loop is enough.
algorithms.sum-average: Accumulate values and compute the mean. See the accumulator pattern that powers many algorithms.
algorithms.loop-explorer: Watch how loop iterations update shared state. See score accumulate with each pass.
algorithms.reverse-list: Two-pointer swap from both ends. Watch pointers move inward until they meet in the middle.
algorithms.palindrome: Compare characters from both ends. See how the two-pointer technique confirms symmetry.
algorithms.fizzbuzz: Classic divisibility check. See modulo drive conditional output across 100 iterations.
algorithms.factorial: Multiply from 1 to n. See the product grow step by step and understand why 0! = 1.
algorithms.fibonacci-iterative: Generate the sequence with two rolling variables. See why this beats the recursive version in space.
algorithms.binary-search: Halve the search space every step. Requires sorted input. Watch O(log n) happen live.
algorithms.selection-sort: Find the minimum each pass and move it to the front. See n passes produce a sorted array.
algorithms.insertion-sort: Insert each element into its correct position in the already-sorted prefix. Efficient for nearly sorted data.
algorithms.two-pointers: Use two indices moving toward each other to solve array problems in O(n) instead of O(n²).
algorithms.hash-map-counting: Use a dictionary to count in O(1) per lookup. The foundation of many frequency problems.
algorithms.stack-ops: LIFO in action. See push, pop, and peek animate on a list used as a stack.
algorithms.queue-ops: FIFO in action. See enqueue and dequeue animate and understand why deque beats a list.
algorithms.anagram-check: Are two strings rearrangements of each other? See character counting solve it in O(n).
algorithms.sliding-window: Find the maximum sum in every window of size k. Watch the window glide across the array.
algorithms.merge-sorted: Combine two sorted arrays into one. The core operation behind merge sort.
algorithms.bubble-sort: Compare adjacent pairs. Larger elements bubble to the top each pass.
algorithms.merge-sort: Divide, sort halves, merge. See the recursion tree split and recombine.
algorithms.quick-sort: Choose a pivot, partition around it, recurse. Average O(n log n) with great cache performance.
algorithms.heap-sort: Build a max-heap, extract elements in order. Guaranteed O(n log n) unlike quicksort.
algorithms.bfs: Explore a graph level by level using a queue. Find shortest paths in unweighted graphs.
algorithms.dfs: Explore as deep as possible before backtracking. See the call stack grow with each recursive step.
algorithms.binary-tree-traversal: In-order, pre-order, post-order. Watch nodes visit in different sequences on the same tree.
algorithms.two-sum: Find two numbers that add to a target. See how a hash map turns O(n²) into O(n).
algorithms.valid-parentheses: Use a stack to match open and close brackets. Classic stack application interview question.
algorithms.fibonacci-recursive: See the call tree fan out exponentially. Understand why memoization is essential.
algorithms.dijkstra: Find shortest paths from a source to all nodes using a priority queue. The backbone of GPS navigation.
algorithms.knapsack: Maximise value within a weight limit. See the DP table fill row by row.
algorithms.lcs: Find the longest subsequence shared by two strings. Core of diff tools and DNA alignment.
algorithms.topological-sort: Order tasks respecting dependencies. See Kahn's algorithm remove nodes with zero in-degree.
algorithms.kruskals: Build a minimum spanning tree by greedily adding lowest-weight edges without forming cycles.
algorithms.trie: Insert and search strings letter by letter. See how autocomplete works under the hood.
algorithms.floyd-warshall: All-pairs shortest paths with a 3-loop DP. See the distance matrix update in O(V³).
algorithms.segment-tree: Range queries and point updates in O(log n). See the tree build and propagate sums upward.
algorithms.coin-change: Minimum coins to make an amount. See the DP array fill from 0 up to the target.
algorithms.bit-manipulation: AND, OR, XOR, shifts — the operations behind cryptography, graphics, and competitive programming.
